_comment: What this repo puts in the chuk-datasets catalog (chuk-datasets.fly.dev).
Register with the shared tool, which lives with the server that owns the
identity algorithm so there is exactly one implementation of it:
uv run ... register datasets.json        # needs CHUK_DATASETS_API_KEY
IMPORTANT, and different from v-tokenizers' entry: `root` here is
gitignored. training/data/ is generated by build_mathonly_corpus.py, not
committed -- 29MB of regenerable JSONL. So this repo deliberately does NOT
run `register.py verify` in CI: a fresh checkout has no files to hash and
the job would fail for the wrong reason. Verification here happens at
registration time and at train time (the corpus guard in train_mathonly.py
refuses ids outside the model's vocabulary), not in CI.
Classes are the spec's enum: pretrain-stream | eval-set | probe-corpus |
midtrain-corpus | raw-source. This is Act 3's midtrain mixture, so
midtrain-corpus -- matching cells/cn7-midtrain-corpus, which is the same

datasets.name: tiny-model/mathonly-midtrain
datasets.description: Act 3's maths-only (zero cell content) midtrain mixture for TinyModel v11: Tier A arithmetic drill at 55% plus TinyStories replay at 45%, tokenized with the published v11 build (vocab 71,260). The clean S1+S4 control arm CN-7's write-up asks for.

generator.note: CORRECTED 2026-07-25, then FIXED. The drill half was always deterministic -- pure-python RNG at seed 90, bit-identical across machines. The replay half was not: it streamed TinyStories through datasets' shuffle(seed=90, buffer_size=10000), whose reservoir depends on shard arrival, so a rebuild yielded a slightly different replay set every time (1,521,190 vs 1,521,059 tokens; 96,889 vs 96,890 rows across two builds of the same command). Because train_mathonly.py takes its validation slice as the last 10% of replay rows, that difference changed the VALIDATION SET -- 663 rows on one build, 710 on another -- which was most of a 1.6079-vs-1.4904 val-NLL gap first blamed on MPS-vs-CUDA. The shuffle is now a seeded stride over the UNSHUFFLED pinned revision, and an M3 and a Colab T4 have independently produced these exact bytes. The corpus stays registered anyway, and that history is why: the seed was assumed to be the identity for months and was not one. Fetching bytes against a sha is.

composition.measured_note: Re-measured 2026-07-27 from the registered ff7bf26b bytes by publish_corpus_hf.py, which derives every number in the dataset card from the corpus rather than from this file. replay_tokens and total_rows previously carried the pre-fix build's values (1,521,190 and 96,889) and had drifted from the bytes they describe. Drill and replay are separated here by EOS, which is exact, rather than by the trainer's len(ids) > 40 proxy -- see validation_split below.
composition.note: add and sub are drawn twice as often as the rest. Operand ranges are CN-7's s1_item verbatim (add/sub 0-99, mul half times-tables half 1-digit x 2-digit, mod 0-99 mod 2-12, cmp/parity/min3 0-999) -- this file's S1 is a copy of that generator, so the two arms differ by the cell species and nothing else.

surfaces.note: Each fact appears across several phrasings with the answer sometimes leading and the operands sometimes reversed. Not decoration: with one template and fixed slots the cheapest thing to memorise is the STRING, which would make the held-out probe below meaningless.

published.note: The same bytes as this catalog entry, on the Hub so someone who watched the video can fetch them without a catalog key. Verified after push by downloading what the Hub serves into a clean directory and recomputing content_sha over it. Fetch the two files by name with hf_hub_download, NOT with `hf download --local-dir`: content_sha is over a directory, and that CLI writes a .cache/ metadata tree beside the files even with --include, which hashes to a9d67ca6 instead of ff7bf26b. Nothing errors -- the trainer runs either way -- so the wrong identity is only found by whatever recomputes it later. The paired cells arm is at chrishayuk/v11-cells-midtrain-corpus.

validation_split.derivation: last 10% of rows with len(ids) > 40, as train_mathonly.py takes it
validation_split.note: Published in the CELLS repo because a worker running that arm never holds this corpus and cannot derive the split. Recorded here because the rows come out of THESE bytes. KNOWN WRINKLE, measured 2026-07-27: len(ids) > 40 is a proxy for 'came from TinyStories', and 213 of the 90,000 narrative drill rows exceed it, so 20 of the 710 validation rows are arithmetic drill items rather than stories (2.8%). They are excluded from training, so this is not leakage -- but a figure reported as 'story replay NLL' is measured on 690 stories and 20 sums. Both arms score the identical published file, so the paired comparison is unaffected; the absolute value carries the caveat. Left as-is deliberately: changing the split changes this file's sha and makes every completed run incomparable.

held_out.note: Withheld from every surface in both orders, so a held-out fact cannot leak via commutativity. Included in this dataset's identity on purpose -- a corpus is not fully described without knowing what was deliberately kept out of it. The probe (training/heldout_probe_mathonly.py) additionally scores the ~982 facts that go unseen naturally.

termination.note: The registered R1 remediation ('add S1 EOS supervision'). Without it, free-running generation ran on into a template-echo mode and P-b read 0.111 against 0.91/0.97 teacher-forced on the same checkpoint. Replay rows are whole TinyStories and stay unterminated, so story generation is unchanged.

tokenizer.name: v11
tokenizer.note: The published build (HF chrishayuk/v11-tokenizer, PyPI v11-tokenizer, crates.io v11-core). Rows are pre-tokenized, so nothing in the bytes records which tokenizer produced them -- this field is how that is recoverable, and train_mathonly.py refuses any corpus whose ids fall outside the model's vocabulary.

replay_source.note: Same pinned revision the base model was pretrained on, so replay is genuinely replay rather than new data.

base_model.note: The checkpoint this corpus mid-trains. Recorded here because the pair is what a result is about; neither alone reproduces anything.

related.note: CN-7 trained S1+S2+S3+S4 together. This is S1+S4 only -- the maths-only control its next_action asks for. Its S1 is 90,000 rows / 1,662,749 tokens against this one's 90,000 / 1,859,026; the difference is the added surfaces and EOS.
